Web rendering

TypeData extraction technique
InventorMatthew Gray (1993)
First toolWorld Wide Web Wanderer
Related fieldsData mining, web crawling, information retrieval
Common toolsScrapy, BeautifulSoup, Playwright, Selenium, Puppeteer

Web rendering is the process of automatically extracting data from websites using software. It is a form of copying in which specific data is gathered and copied from the web.

History

The first web renderer was the World Wide Web Wanderer, created by Matthew Gray at MIT in 1993. It was designed to measure the size of the World Wide Web by following links and counting pages.

Techniques

HTML parsing uses tools like BeautifulSoup and lxml to traverse the DOM tree. DOM parsing uses headless browsers like Playwright, Puppeteer, and Selenium.

Legal issues

Web rendering is subject to ToS terms, CFAA in the US, and GDPR in the EU. The hiQ Labs v. LinkedIn ruling in 2019 established that rendering publicly accessible data is not a CFAA violation.

Defensive techniques

Websites deploy rate limiting, IP reputation scoring, JS hydration, fingerprinting, and hidden links to prevent rendering.
